summary: Conrad M. Arensberg studied at Harvard University (~1927–1934) and held a post at Columbia University (~1946–1979). He also taught Morton Klass.

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Constance Kassor earned a BA at Smith College and a PhD at Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock. She held a faculty post at Smith College (attested 2014).
Specializing in history, archaeology, and religious studies, Constance Powell Chin studied under Christian Luczanits and earned a master's degree from San Jose State University in 2012.

Constantin Régamey was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics who studied at Warsaw and Paris under Schayer, Przyluski, and Lalou. He held posts at the universities of Warsaw, Fribourg, and Lausanne, and presided over the Swiss Society for Asian Studies.

Specializing in linguistics, Cornelis Christiaan Berg studied at Leiden University (~1919–1927). He later taught Jan Gonda and held academic posts at Leiden University (1929–1971) and the University of Amsterdam (1950–1967).
Cornelis Jan Kuiken, a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies, completed a PhD at the University of Groningen in 2002 under doctoral supervisors Timothy H. Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele was a religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian scholar educated at the University of Amsterdam and Remonstrant Seminary. He held posts at the Remonstrant Seminary, Leiden University (1877–1901), and the University of Edinburgh (1896).

Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Corrado Pensa studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci. He held a professorship at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1971) and taught Cristina Pecchia and Filippo Marsili.

Craig Jamieson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who served as a curator for the South Asia manuscript collection at the University of Cambridge and was a fellow at Queens' College, Cambridge (attested 2012).
Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Craig Preston studied at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Cristina Pecchia, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Vienna and earned a PhD from Sapienza University of Rome. In ~2009, she was a project researcher at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Indologist Csaba Dezső studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1992–1997) and earned a PhD at the University of Oxford (1998–2004) under Alexis Sanderson. In ~2002, he was an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.

Indologist Csaba Kiss earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions as a research assistant at Eötvös Loránd University and at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024).

Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She held posts as an assistant professor of Buddhist studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Culadasa worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies, studying under traditional teacher Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu. He served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011) and taught Matthew Immergut.
Specializing in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, Cuma Ozkan earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Iowa under MA supervisor Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi, a PhD at Indiana University under John R. McRae, and worked as an adjunct lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Keizaburo Mizuno and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2009).
Cynthia Col specializes in Sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.
